terms.meaning: A log line with named fields in a fixed format, such as JSON, so tools can search it.
A separate output channel used for error messages, often shown in red or sent to a different place.

sections.name: Fields
sections.title: Fields type
sections.what: Defines what a set of log fields is: a simple collection of named values.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeping fields loose lets each caller add its own details.
sections.watch_out: Any value can go in, including personal data, so callers must check what they pass.

sections.name: write
sections.title: Line writer
sections.what: Writes one JSON line with the level, message, time and fields. Errors go to the error stream and other levels to the normal output.
sections.why: The comment on the module says logs are structured JSON, and splitting errors out is a common convention.
sections.watch_out: Some hosting tools only show the normal output by default, so errors may need a separate check.

sections.name: log
sections.title: Logger functions
sections.what: Provides three functions, info, warn and error, that each write a line at their level.
sections.why: Gives the rest of the app one simple, consistent way to log.
sections.watch_out: A warning goes to the normal output, not the error stream, so it is easy to miss when only errors are watched.

summary: Writes simple structured log lines in JSON, with errors going to the error stream and everything else to the normal output stream.
purpose: Gives the app a consistent, searchable record of what happens on the server, without printing free text.
why: The header says never to pass secrets or personal data in fields. The choice of JSON lines is stated in the file's design, which suits log tools.
how: 1) Takes a message and a set of fields. 2) Adds the level and the time, and writes one JSON line. 3) Sends errors to the error stream and other levels to the normal stream. 4) Exposes info, warn and error functions.
inputs: A message text and optional fields, which are plain values.
outputs: One JSON line per call, written to the console or log collection.
risks: Fields are written exactly as passed, with no removal of secrets or personal data, so the caller must avoid them. Error objects do not turn into useful text unless the message is extracted first.
debug: If logs are missing, check whether they were sent to the error stream, which some tools do not show by default. If a line looks wrong, check that the fields are plain values, not error objects.
